topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture by framing the importance, complexity, and historical context of the complement system within immunology.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core principles, naming conventions, and central pivotal role of C3 activation in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three distinct recognition pathways that initiate complement and converge to form surface-bound C3 convertase.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream processes through which activated complement eradicates pathogens via opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the regulatory factors and mechanisms that protect host cells from inappropriate complement activation and destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical presentations and autoimmune or infectious pathologies that arise from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to circumvent complement attack.

topics.label: Lecture closing and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and outlines the next topic covering the adaptive immune system.
